body:
Hi @dmaicher, thanks for reporting this issue.

You're right, this commit breaks the calls to data transformers, there is nothing wrong with your code.

I'm working on a new patch though. Changing to a `POST_SET_DATA` event is indeed a possible workaround.

Sorry for that, it will be fixed very soon!

Please also note that it's not the proper way to fix this regression, because any choice would never be pre selected by the data mapper. In your case it's the first entity so you won't see any difference.

In fact, I just realise something about your code. Since you're defining `choices` options, you don't need to use the `EntityType` which is made to load choices from `class` option. You should use directly the `ChoiceType` instead.

So, if I understand correctly you just want to select the first option ? So you should do it with the `data` option:

``` php
$field = $builder->create('individualQuestionOptions', 'choice', array(
    'choices' => $choices = $question->getIndividualQuestionOptions(),
    'expanded' => true,
    'data' => $choices->first(),
));
```

Could you please try this code which removes not needed options without your data transformer ?

Thanks for the fast reply ;)

Well I think I will need a DataTransformer because in the model its always a Collection. In some cases I want to display radio buttons where users can only select exactly one entity with `'multiple' => false`. So I will have to transform the selected entity to a Collection with one element and vice versa.

@dmaicher `ChoiceType` supports `\Traversable` like `ArrayCollection`. The `EntityType` is just an "extension" to load choices. If choices are already loaded the last one is useless.
In your case you already defines `choices` options so you should do it directly on the `ChoiceType` since the logic of `EntityType` is not used and `multiple` option is false by default.

Defining which choice is pre selected can be done with the `data` option. `DataTransformers` should only be used to handle specific normalized data or view data but the `ArrayChoiceList` is already some kind of "choice to value" transformer.

The responsible commit for your bug just moved the related wrapped transformation logic from the `RadioListMapper` to a listener of `PRE_SET_DATA` event.

> The responsible commit for your bug just moved the related wrapped transformation logic from the RadioListMapper to a listener of PRE_SET_DATA event.

Wich is wrong by the way

Well I think I cannot "just" use `ChoiceType` because how would it know how to transform an entity to an ID for the view and an ID back to an entity when coming from the view? That's pretty much why I use the `EntityType`.

So `$question->getIndividualQuestionOptions()` is actually an ArrayCollection that contains entities.

I would have to add some logic then via transformers or existing options (like `'choice_value'`)?

This:

``` php
$field = $builder->create('individualQuestionOptions', 'choice', array(
    'data_class' => IndividualQuestionOption::class,
    'multiple' => false,
    'expanded' => true,
    'auto_initialize' => false,
    'choices' => $question->getIndividualQuestionOptions(),
    'translation_domain' => 'validators',
    'empty_value' => false,
));
```

leads to:

`The value of type "object" cannot be converted to a valid array key.`

By default it will use an incrementing index for view value, but you can indeed set it to the id with a string property path or a closure:

``` php
$field = $builder->create('individualQuestionOptions', 'choice', array(
    'choices' => $choices = $question->getIndividualQuestionOptions(),
    'choice_value' => 'id', // will call $choice->getId(),
    // or
    'choice_value' => function ($choice) { return $choice->getId(); },
    'expanded' => true,
    'data' => $choices->first(), // pre select first choice calling $form->setData($choices->first())
));
```

But you're right, in your case calling `$form->getData()` will return a single entity which you would need to wrap in an `ArrayCollection`, so if you don't want to do that when handling data after submission (in a controller ?) you would need a transformer as you're doing.

I really don't think you need `EntityType`.

Sorry for messing with the transformers with that commit. I was not sure about it though, thanks again for pointing this out.

Note that there is already a transformer so you don't need to code one, however it's only added by default when `EntityType` is multiple: `Symfony\Bridge\Form\DataTransformer\CollectionToArrayTransformer`

Ok at least this renders the page again :)

``` php
$field = $builder->create('individualQuestionOptions', 'choice', array(
    'data_class' => IndividualQuestionOption::class,
    'multiple' => false,
    'expanded' => true,
    'auto_initialize' => false,
    'choices' => $question->getIndividualQuestionOptions(),
    'translation_domain' => 'validators',
    'empty_value' => false,
    'choices_as_values' => true,
));
```

Submitting does not work though because it tries to set an entity on the model but the model expects a collection (thats why I had the transformer).

If I add back the transformer then it seems to work though:

``` php
$field->addModelTransformer(new ChoiceToQuestionOptionTransformer());
```

Although it should also work with the `EntityType` even if its not needed here? :)
To me its seems a bit as a BC break but maybe I was just using the `entity` type wrong ;P

The Form Component has evolved a lot with 2.7 and 2.8, you should read the corresponding upgrade files since there are indeed a few BC breaks.

Thank you for your feedback, I may need it again to confirm my patch will work for your use case :)
